summary: You send a prompt, stare at a blank screen, and then the whole answer drops at once. The AI apps you use every day avoid that by streaming the answer word by word, and you can build the same thing into your own agents. Why AI apps show their answers word by word, and how to build that into your own agents. A language model already generates its answer one token at a time, each token predicted from everything before it. Streaming just sends each token the moment it's generated instead of waiting for the whole response. The model isn't any faster, but time to first token (TTFT) drops, so the app feels much quicker. Under the hood, the connection between your app and the server stays open, and the server pushes each token through it as it's produced, usually over HTTP streaming or Server-Sent Events (SSE). summary: Pasting the same error back and saying "still broken, try again" gives your agent nothing new, so it starts guessing. Give it what you expected, what actually happened, and the full error, and it has somewhere to start. Vibe coding is great until the errors start piling up. You paste the error in, ask for a fix, it doesn't work, you say "try again," and the agent keeps guessing because you haven't given it anything new. Sometimes it rewrites the whole file, sometimes it fixes the original bug and quietly creates a new one. The fix starts with better information. Tell the agent what you expected and what happened instead (you clicked save, the button spun, the request returned a 500, nothing was saved), and include the whole error message and stack trace even if you don't understand every line. For visual bugs, attach a screenshot. Before it changes any code, talk the problem through with it first. Adding "don't change anything yet" keeps an enthusiastic agent from rewriting things while you test one idea at a time. Follow AWS Developers! summary: Today we're announcing AWS Emulator. Build and test your AWS applications on your own machine, before you deploy. AWS Emulator is for development and testing. Once it's installed, you don't need network access or an AWS account, and there's no additional service fee. Each instance gets its own port, keys and state, so your coding agents and CI pipelines don't share resources.
